transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you for seeing me. Um, well, I guess I'm here because... I've been having a little bit of trouble lately with, um, eating. It's probably not a huge deal, but sometimes at night when I'm alone, I just sort of... keep eating. It's like I get carried away, you know? I'll be telling myself I should probably stop and put the food away, but it just feels a bit hard to actually do it in the moment. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
When you find yourself eating past the point where you feel full or think you should stop, does it feel like you can’t control how much you eat or stop eating once you’ve started?

Um, yeah... I guess that's exactly it. I mean, I don't want to make it sound way worse than it is—I'm not going crazy or anything—but... yeah. Once I start eating alone at night, it just sort of feels like... like something else takes over. 

I'll literally be standing there, in my head, telling myself to just put the food away, but I just can't seem to make myself actually stop. It's a little embarrassing to admit that out loud, honestly. Am I explaining that right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel distressed or upset about these episodes of eating past the point of fullness, or has this behavior affected your daily life in any way?

Um... well, I try not to let it get to me too much. I'm sure everyone overeats and gets a little upset about it sometimes, right? But... yeah, I guess it is starting to bother me a bit more. 

I feel a little bad admitting this, but it actually kind of affected my work recently. I'm an animal caretaker, and we do these community events... and the other day, I was doing this bilingual outreach presentation. I should have been completely focused, but I just got so distracted thinking about leaving afterward and... going home to get food. I ended up kind of stumbling through parts of the talk. 

I mean, I don't think it was a complete disaster or anything! But... I was really worried my coworkers might have noticed I was messing up. I always try to be really dependable at work, so that was... a little hard for me to deal with. Did I explain that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
How often would you say these episodes of not being able to stop eating once you start happen?

Um... well, it's not like it's every single night, you know? I'm usually pretty good during the week. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, for the last four months or so, it's been happening maybe... at least once a week? Where I'm alone and I just eat way more than I planned. 

And, um... I really hope you don't think less of me for this, but... sometimes, after I do that, I get so anxious about it that I... I make myself throw up. Just to kind of fix it, I guess. I know it sounds terrible, and I try not to do it, but... yeah. Is that... is that the kind of detail you needed? I'm sorry if that's too much information.
Have you been making yourself vomit or doing anything else, like exercising a lot or using laxatives, to try to 'undo' the effects of eating more than you planned?

Um... yeah. Like I mentioned just a second ago, I do... I do make myself throw up. I really don't want you to think I'm doing it all the time or that I'm completely out of control, because I'm not. It's just... after I eat like that, I usually end up in the bathroom doing it because it just feels like the only way to, you know, undo it before the calories settle in. 

I don't use laxatives or exercise for hours and hours or anything extreme like that! It's just the throwing up. I know it's not a good habit, and I'm really trying to be better about it. I hope that's okay to admit... I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right. Is that what you were asking?
